label: Sensor traits
description: Always-on ways a unit finds enemies or hides from them, on top of its sight band. They need no key; the same effects on a key are patterns (cloak, reveal an area, mark a target, jam sensors, fire countermeasures). For source units, list only the traits the stock unit has whatever its loadout. A sensor from a loadout pick, an upgrade or veterancy goes in sensors.notes. Never add a trait as a proposal.

terms.label: Radar
terms.description: Shows enemies in a wide circle beyond its sight as blips on the team's minimap: where they are, not what they are. A blip can't be aimed at until someone sees it, and stealthy enemies don't show.

terms.label: Detector
terms.description: Reveals stealthy, cloaked, burrowed and disguised enemies close to it, for the whole team.

terms.label: Stealth
terms.description: Hard to spot: enemies see it only at close range, and radar never shows it. Firing gives it away for a moment, and a detector nearby reveals it.
terms.notes: Always on. Turning fully invisible, on a key or not, is the cloak pattern.

terms.label: Lingering sight
terms.description: Enemies it sees stay marked for the whole team for a few seconds after they leave its sight, visible through walls and fog while the mark lasts.
terms.notes: Unlike the mark weapon trait, it marks everything it sees, not only what it hits, and adds no extra damage. Not the spotter team-play hook, which covers any way of spotting for the team.

terms.label: Jammer
terms.description: Hides itself and allies close to it from radar and lock-ons: they show on no minimap and can be targeted only by sight.
terms.notes: Always on. A jamming bubble on a key is the jam-sensors pattern; flares or chaff fired on a key to break a lock are the fire-countermeasures pattern.
examples: MechWarrior Online: the Guardian ECM hides the mech and nearby allies from enemy sensors
